                    ### Question
                    For which of the following patients would you recommend prophylaxis against mycobacterium avium-intracellulare?

                    ### Options
                    opa. 22-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 750 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 500,000 copies/mL
opb. 30-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 20 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
opc. 45-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 250 cells/ microliter and a viral load of 100,000 copies/mL
opd. 50-year old HIV positive female with CD4 count of 150 cells/ microliter and a viral load of < 50 copies/mL
ope. 36-year old HIV positive male with CD4 count of 75 cells/microliter and an undetectable viral load.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare is recommended for patients with low CD4 counts (<50 cells/microliter) due to significantly increased risk of opportunistic infections. This recommendation is supported by the consensus that low CD4 counts increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections, including Mycobacterium avium Complex. Therefore, the 30-year old HIV positive male with a CD4 count of 20 cells/microliter (option b) would benefit from prophylaxis.
